newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's Manitoba expects robust economy in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Manitoba expects robust economy in 1997.

text.p: Strong economic growth was expected to continue into the new year in Canada's western province of Manitoba, a provincial government statement said.

"In the past year we've seen the Manitoba economy surge ahead. Industries such as manufacturing, tourism and agriculture are gearing up for growth. Investment, exports and GDP are all on the rise. The economic momentum is strong and we have every reason to believe it will continue in 1997," Manitoba Industry Minister Jim Downey said.
Agriculture, Manitoba's top export sector, saw farm cash receipts rise 12.4 percent.
Exports of all goods to the United States rose 10.9 percent by the end of October compared to the same period last year. Exports to the United States more than doubled between 1990 and 1995.
Gross domestic product was expected to grow 2.8 percent in 1996 compared to the national forecast of 1.6 percent, the Conference Board of Canada said.
Private capital investment rose 3.9 percent as Manitoba was the only province to record five consecutive years of private investment capital growth.
Retail sales by October 31 outpaced the national rate of 2.2 percent by more than two and a half times at 5.9 percent.
Tourism saw its fifth consecutive year of growth and generated more than C$1.0 billion as visitors from the United States rose 3.3 percent.
